concepts.definition: A four-legged part that puts three LEDs, red, green and blue, in one case.
concepts.example: By driving the three channels separately from D9, D10 and D11 you get any colour you want.
concepts.pitfall: Mixing up the channels' R, G, B legs; the colours come out different from what you expect, so check the wire ends.

concepts.definition: The type where the cathodes of the three LEDs join at one leg; the COM leg is connected to GND.
concepts.example: With COM on GND, analogWrite(9, 255) lights the red channel at full brightness.
concepts.pitfall: Connecting the COM leg of a common cathode LED to 5V; COM only goes to 5V on a common anode LED.

concepts.definition: In light, colours add up: red + green gives yellow, red + green + blue gives white.
concepts.pitfall: Comparing light mixing with paint mixing; paints get darker as you mix them, light gets lighter.

concepts.definition: The type where the anodes of the three LEDs join at one leg; COM goes to 5V and a channel lights while its pin is LOW.
concepts.example: To light a channel at brightness 200, you write analogWrite(pin, 255 - 200).
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to write the values the other way round on a common anode LED; you ask for red and see cyan.

concepts.definition: Keeps a value between a given lower and upper limit.
concepts.pitfall: Writing Serial.parseInt() straight inside constrain; the expression may run several times and read extra numbers from serial. Store it in a variable first.

quiz.prompt: You are using a common cathode RGB LED. Where should the COM leg be connected?
quiz.explanation: With a common cathode, the cathodes of the three LEDs join at COM, and the cathode is the GND side. So COM goes to GND and the channels light up with the HIGH coming from the PWM pins. Connecting it to 5V is for a common anode LED.
Red is off, green and blue are fully on. In light, colours add up: green + blue gives cyan. Yellow is red + green, purple is red + blue, and white is all three fully on.

quiz.prompt: You want to light the red channel of a common anode RGB LED at a brightness of 200/255. With a common anode the logic flips. Which value should you give analogWrite?
quiz.explanation: With a common anode a channel lights while its pin is LOW, so the value is written the other way round: 255 - 200 = 55. If you write 200, the channel only lights at about 22% brightness.

options: setup() is empty: analogWrite does not work because pinMode is missing
The for condition i <= 3: the arrays have 3 elements, and when i = 3 the program reads outside the array
The analogWrite(10, ...) line: it should say D12 for green
delay(1000): too long for an RGB LED
quiz.explanation: The valid indexes of a 3-element array are 0, 1, 2. With i <= 3, the last round reads a memory value outside the array, such as kirmizi[3]; a random colour comes out. The correct condition is i < 3. analogWrite makes the pin an output by itself, D10 is the right green pin, and the delay time is not a problem.

quiz.prompt: The blue channel's forward voltage is 3.0 V. With 5 V and 330 Ω, how many mA flow through the channel when the pin is fully HIGH? (Simple formula: I = (5 - Vf) / R; ignore the internal resistance of the pin and the LED.)
quiz.explanation: I = (5 - 3.0) / 330 = 2 / 330, about 0.00606 A, that is 6.06 mA. The lab model also adds the internal resistance of the pin and the LED and gets about 5.6 mA. On the red channel Vf is smaller (1.9 V) and the current is bigger, about 9.4 mA.
